definitions.explanation: The act of intentionally passing over parts of a text without reading them carefully or at all.

examples.japanese: {規約|きやく}は{読|よ}み{飛|と}ばしがちだ。
examples.english: People tend to skim over the terms of service.

examples.japanese: {読|よ}み{飛|と}ばしをすると{大事|だいじ}な{情報|じょうほう}を{見落|みお}とす。
examples.english: If you skim, you'll miss important information.

examples.japanese: {長|なが}い{小説|しょうせつ}を{読|よ}むとき、{退屈|たいくつ}な{場面|ばめん}は{読|よ}み{飛|と}ばしをしてしまうことがある。
examples.english: When reading a long novel, I sometimes end up skipping over the boring scenes.

notes:
The noun form of the verb {読|よ}み{飛|と}ばす (to skim; to skip while reading). Describes the action of deliberately not reading parts of a text, whether out of impatience, disinterest, or efficiency.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {読|よ}み{飛|と}ばしをする: to do skimming; to skip parts
- {読|よ}み{飛|と}ばしがちだ: tend to skim over
- {読|よ}み{飛|と}ばし{禁止|きんし}: no skipping (instruction)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {斜|なな}め{読|よ}み: skimming; reading diagonally — implies scanning quickly for key points rather than skipping entirely
- {飛|と}ばし{読|よ}み: skip-reading — same meaning, reversed word order; less common
- {速読|そくどく}: speed reading — a technique for reading quickly while maintaining comprehension
